title: April: Planning My Exit
coreMove: A lower-cost life turns savings into runway: when expenses, client income, dates, and support are visible, leaving misfit work becomes a plan instead of a fantasy.

exampleSpecs.audience: employee preparing for a career change
exampleSpecs.stakes: The April emergency fund must become runway instead of vague comfort.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tie extra savings to a real exit decision.

exampleSpecs.audience: writers moving from salary to client work
exampleSpecs.stakes: September 1 must become a planned date, not a daydream.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Compare real expenses with possible client income.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Remote work and long hours are being mistaken for dedication.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Name burnout as misalignment, not laziness.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A growing startup can become wrong before the title changes.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Treat rigidity and disconnection as evidence about fit.

exampleSpecs.stakes: July 1 should stay a stretch only if client income supports it.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use two dates to separate ambition from evidence.

exampleSpecs.audience: workers worried about explaining a career shift
exampleSpecs.stakes: A father's reassurance should strengthen preparation, not replace it.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use support to confirm a prepared career change.
